#3716. Overwatch doesn’t have ‘any intention’ of making 6-vs-6 the main mode, but it’s now ‘a second among equals’

The never-ending battle between Overwatch players choosing five-vs-five or six-vs-six will rage on.

In a new Director’s Take blog today, game director Aaron Keller confirmed that Overwatch will continue to support both formats, but with a renewed focus on the classic six-vs-six, which the studio is “starting to think of it as a second among equals.”

“We always say that we want to make the game you all want to play and it’s obvious that we have folks who want different things,” Keller said, citing player surveys that were very split between the two options, as seen above. “Over the past few years, we’ve realized that there doesn’t have to be a ‘winner’ between five-vs-five and six-vs-six. The real competition should be in your matches, not between two modes that can coexist. You can play either one (many people actually play both!) and we’re going to support that choice.”

Personally? I’m a fan of six-vs-six, but that’s because I’m a tank main. Solo tanking is a pain compared to having a buddy on the frontline with you, and I can see that there are many who agree with me…but also many who don’t. Overwatch will continue to feature both, Keller says, and there won’t be any radical switches soon either, other than an additional six-vs-six queue.

“Six-vs-six has been slowly growing in popularity over the last few years; however, the five-vs-five version of Open Queue was popular too,” Keller said. “We’d like to learn how many people are playing Open Queue six-vs-six for the role flexibility and how many people are playing it for the team size. Running both modes at the same time should produce some good data points to show us where we ought to be putting more energy.”

Keller warned that adding the new queue (Role Queue six-vs-six) instead of replacing an old one may impact queue times, but it “should be better overall for our community.” He also said that the team theorizes that some matchmaking changes coming in season six “will keep queue times more manageable” alongside the new option.

“We’ll put more energy into balance patches for [six-vs-six] and we’ll continue to look for the right format that really gives our community the experience they’re looking for,” Keller said. “Whether that’s Open Queue, Role Queue, a combination of both, or a new format that we’ve yet to try out, we’re here to figure out what works best for you.”

Being a struggling actor in Hollywood is tough, and even huge stars like Chris Pratt go through the wringer early in their careers (like working at Bubba Gump Shrimp). Such was the case when Pratt lost out on the titular role on the show Chuck. Pratt auditioned for the role in 2007, but lost it to Zachary Levi. That has got to be hard enough, but for Pratt, it was made worse as he was taunted by a billboard for the show in LA. Pratt got the last laugh on the casting directors of the show years later when he got his own poster on the same building for Jurassic World.

After trying out for and not making the final cut for Chuck, things got worse when a billboard Pratt could see from his apartment went up advertising the show, with Levi featured on it. Pratt recently talked about it with Barstool:

I did a screen test for Chuck. I wanted it so bad, and then there was this giant billboard across from my apartment of Zach Levi as Chuck, and I’m like, ‘grrr.’

Imagine waking up every morning and looking out the window at a billboard that you hoped would have your face on it, only to see someone else you lost out to. It would be maddening! Pratt kept at it, of course, and eventually landed gigs in Jennifer’s Body and Moneyball, before really breaking big as part of the ensemble cast of Parks and Rec. It wasn’t until 2015 when the moment came full circle, at the premiere of one of Pratt’s earliest blockbusters, Jurassic World.

The moment wasn’t lost on Pratt, as he explained:

Then that same building is where we had the premiere for Jurassic World. And that same building had a giant poster on it with me on a motorcycle, and I was like, 'whoa!'

That really is coming full circle, from what sounds like a real low point early in his career to the triumph of starring in one of the biggest franchises in Hollywood history. Jurassic World came right on the heels of Pratt joining the MCU as Star-Lord in the first Guardians of the Galaxy, so he had become one of the biggest movie stars on the planet.

So does this mean he’s got a “hidden rivalry” with Levi? Well, probably not. He doesn’t seem to have an animosity towards the Shazam! star, just frustration for not getting a part at that point in his career. It’s safe to say that things have worked out pretty well for Pratt, who will next be seen on the 2026 movie schedule in Way of the Warrior Kid, which will be available to watch with an Apple TV subscription.

#3712. Nintendo Shuts Down Switch 2 Jailbreak, Sending Hackers Back To Square One

On October 22, news broke that the Switch 2 had been jailbroken for the first time. This meant that it wasâkindaâpossible to mod and dump games on the machine, which in the past would have opened the floodgates to third-party operating systems being installed and an accessible piracy scene. But not this time. Due to the incredibly complicated nature of the jailbreak, the need for now-delisted sofrware SmileBASIC, and that it was software based rather than hardware, Nintendo has been able to shut it down with its latest firmware update.

In the past, Nintendo’s portable consoles have become enormously popular among homebrew developers and the piracy scene for the ease with which they could be adapted. The Nintendo DS (its most successful console until the Switch, selling 154 million units and just shy of a billion games) had the infamous R4 cart onto which ROMs could be installed, while the original model of the Nintendo Switch (157 million units, 1.6 billion games) could be jailbroken due to a hardware issue that Nintendo couldn’t patch out. These exploits didn’t appear to hinder the consoles’ successes, but Nintendo remains resolute in its fury against such actions.

By October 26, hackers had figured out how to get more out of the Switch 2’s very limited exploit, able to dump games as ROMs and dig into the console’s file systems, which would usually be the beginning of emulation plans and homebrew development. Now, however, as reported by Oatmeal Dome, all this is patched out by the device’s 23.5.0 firmware update.

The OS exploit used in the recent jailbreak has been patched in version 23.5.0.

Dumping and modding games will be impossible again from this point forward, with the exception of some cartridge games (and maybe game updates) that are released in the near future.

— OatmealDome (@OatmealDome) November 10, 2026

This is possible because the issues discovered were software based, rather than something intrinsic to the physical hardware inside the Switch 2, as had been the case for the original model of the Switch 1. There, Nintendo had to change the manufacturing, and there was little that could be done to stop Switch 1 users from taking advantage, so long as they didn’t log in to Nintendo’s online services. Of course, of the tens of millions of people who owned the Switch that could do it, vanishingly few actually did, and software sales broke all of Nintendo’s records.

Eventually the crackers will find a way, because eventually they always do, but in this case it could be many years away.

Also, when the process is ongoing it really alarms my bodyguard, who responds like a dog hearing a bang in the house at night.

#3710. How to change layers in WoW Forever? (After the layer size change)

If you want to play with friends in WoW: Forever, you have to go back to one of WoW's most dreaded concepts - layers and shards.

World of Warcraft: Forever skips realms and introduces gameplay rulesets instead, where you can pick your preferred playstyle and get whisked to an Azeroth populated with like-minded individuals. But things can get complicated if, say, you want to play with your friends or guildmates from across the world.

Plus, it’s not like Blizzard will squeeze everyone using your gameplay ruleset into the same world instance. This is where layers come in, and it’s similar to, but also very different from, its original iteration in Classic.

Others new to WoW might be wondering what exactly layers are, and how they might affect their WoW: Forever experience.

So we know MMOs have servers, and each WoW server has a realm that contains a version of Azeroth and the players inside it. Of course, we can’t expect Blizzard to spawn everyone at once, since we’d overcrowd the game world and break the experience.

When a location gets a high-enough population, WoW uses sharding to copy the area into a “shard” and transfers some players there. A shard is a perfectly working copy of a location, complete with NPCs and objects, except you can only see and interact with players of the same shard.

The idea is to manage overpopulation by keeping player counts at a certain number. This keeps lag manageable and ensures there are enough mobs and quest items for everyone in any given zone.

Since shards are zone-wide, you can see players “disappear” into a new zone because they’re crossing over to a new shard (called phasing). If you’re approaching a zone where all shards are at capacity, you’d hit a soft “loading” queue before you enter. Worst case, you get disconnected from the server, which can ruin your momentum.

WoW Retail still uses sharding. It sometimes implements cross-realm zones (CRZs), so low-population realms can share low-population zones.

We got to layering at the launch of WoW Classic in 2019, where it was presented as a bigger solution to server population. Sharding at the time just didn’t feel like a practical choice, as they’d have to create hundreds of shards per zone.

“We had some serious concerns about what would happen when realms started to mature, and populations shifted,” Blizzard noted about sharding in the release of Battle for Wintergrasp in Wrath Classic. “Would we have hundreds of realms with low populations a few months in?”

So they came up with layers, which is sharding but applied to the whole game world. Upon meeting specific population conditions, Blizzard can create a copy of Azeroth and transfer players there.

But it’s not a perfect solution. Too much layering could result in dead cities, and too little overcrowds areas. It can hurt the economy as well, as you can layer-hop to get more resources from another layer once your layer’s route runs out.

Classic moved away from layering just a few months in November 2019 and converged everyone into a single layer.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Players reintroduced the layering and sharding discourse back into Forever overpopulation concerns during launch. We don’t have the full picture of how Blizzard is managing Forever servers as of writing, but players seem to have noticed enough to make informed assumptions:

Instead of realms, we choose a ruleset that represents our preferred playstyle and play with others who choose the same. In theory, it’s a “realmless” system, and our ruleset of choice is functionally a mega server that our fellow ruleset comrades share.

Forever seems to have retained the Retail sharding system. But this time, there’s a chance you can auto-switch layers during the transition. This seems to have carried over from beta. Redditor u/Kellian noted that per-zone “loading” means hostiles and friendlies phase in and out, and can even stop PvP.

Building upon the ruleset is what Blizzard called the familiar faces system. As explained in their BlizzCon 2026 deep-dive, this will have players more consistently encounter the same strangers throughout their leveling journey. The goal is for these familiar faces to give Forever a stronger sense of community spirit, and may even encourage teaming up while you level. This also extends to guilds, so they can potentially pull you into their layers.

At random intervals during your sessions (sometimes none at all), you might encounter a prompt that warns you of a World Refresh. Either you do the refresh now or wait a couple of minutes. This isn’t any cause for alarm, as it just means the game will transfer you to a new instance or layer.

These refreshes often happen to balance the current population. You remain in the same spot, but your immediate surroundings might be different, like there might be more players, more mobs, or both.

Switching between layers in Forever can be done in a variety of ways, but there’s no manual options button to do so. Instead, you can do some things to “force” your way into a layer switch. Popular methods you can try include:

At launch, game dev Aggrend said they would look into how players lamented how sparsely populated the game world felt. A few days later, some players noticed so many characters for so few mobs.

This was especially challenging in PvP, where one faction can dominate a layer and make it difficult for the opposing one to level up or gather resources.

Redditor u/sknilegap doesn’t even call it layering at all, but actually just sharding. And their problem has less to do with the technology itself, but more with its impact on the experience at large.

“I am fine with the necessity of the system. Just keep it immersive,” they said in their post. “Make me sticky to those crossing over around the same time window as me. So […] we all see each other on the other side of the next zone, grouped or not.”

You can play World of Warcraft: Forever on PC and macOS.

That bonus $20 between the $80 base edition and the Ultimate Edition is counted as "recurrent consumer spending", as is part of that massive bump the company has seen.

It also seems that we will see more GTA games - or content, at least - sooner than expected. "We do think that the nature and velocity of the content we'll see from our iconic franchises, including GTA, will look dramatically different over the next decade." It's a vague comment, but assumedly the work done on the engine and backend of GTA 6 means we'll see more content arriving in shorter order than we're used to for the series. This is per an article published by IGN in line with the earning's call going live.

Elsewhere in the earnings call, Take-Two referred to its current setup with its mobile, sports, 'core new IP' and 'core existing IP' as "the strongest development pipeline in the company's history". In terms of new IP, Zelnick directed investors to consider the launches of incoming projects like Ken Levine's mysterious Judas and Project Ethos (which we don't know too much about yet, other than it's billed as a "roguelike hero shooter"). For core IP, 8 sequels and 7 remakes, remasters, and platform extensions.

Buoyed by these plans, Zelnick outlines that he believes that fiscal year 2027 "will be a historic year for Take-Two" as the company is buoyed by "recent and upcoming releases". No prizes for what that's referring to. If you're curious about what sort of numbers we may be looking at here, all you need to do is cast your mind back to 2014, where you will remember GTA 5 made $1bn in just three days.

#3707. As investors ask about GTA 6 and AI, Take-Two CEO once again puts faith in dev creativity, states making hit games "remains the purview of human beings"

"Making a big hit was hard then, and it's hard now, and it's going to be hard in the future."

Today, as part of Take-Two Interactive Software's Q2 2027 earnings call, Strauss Zelnick fielded questions from investors after presenting the financial results of the company. One caller was concerned about AI - specifically about the proliferation of AI-powered compilations and decompilations that have been raising piracy concerns for publishers over the past few weeks.

Zelnick notes that "[the video games] business has been largely immune to piracy" thanks to factors like file size, how console ecosystems work, and aspects related to the online nature of the games industry. That said, Strauss continues, there is a threat posed to the industry because of AI. However, he assures listening investors that Take-Two is appropriately scaling its measures against bad faith actors using artificial intelligence.

"We are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defences and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And - at the same time, without in any way being cavalier - every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy, [and] this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it."

Zelnick pivots back to AI again later in the call, where one investor once again asks about AI, seemingly keen to learn whether the CEO feels it can provide GTA 6 developer Rockstar with any kind of "competitive advantage" in the games industry. Given Zelnick's previous comments on the subject, his answer was not a complete surprise.

"It's always been true [that technology benefits us]," explains Zelnick. "We've always created our entertainment inside computers with technology. All advances have benefited us, and I don't expect that that will change - in fact, I hope it'll accelerate. I think at the same time, what we're known for [at Take-Two] is the desire to make the best entertainment on Earth. And, more often than not, we have succeeded - and the creativity that drives that success is human creativity harnessing technology. And I think that's what you'll see in the future, too.

"Undoubtedly some of the most recent technological advances that you've seen have made it easier to create assets. Where all that is consistent with the story of our business. When I started in interactive entertainment (longer ago than I would like to say), it was really difficult to create an asset in a computer. Today, it's a whole lot easier - but you know what's not easier? Making a big hit. Making a big hit was hard then, and it's hard now, and it's going to be hard in the future. And hit creation remains the purview of human beings."

This isn't the first instance of AI skepticism we've seen from Strauss Zelnick. Back in March, he outright rejected the idea that AI can tackle games on the scale of GTA 6. Elsewhere in the call, the Take-Two CEO reiterated how well GTA 6 is tracking as he reasserted pre-order numbers are well above expectations, and promised that the success of the game will "set a new baseline" for Take-Two's gaming business.

Minor spoilers ahead for the most recent episode of Survivor.

The Open Era of Survivor is here, with new episodes of the 51st season airing weekly on CBS (and streaming with a Paramount+ subscription). While some fans have complained about twists, I'm enjoying this season, especially certain characters like Kristin Flickinger. She recently got some backlash after opting out of eating two grubs in the last episode, and took to social media to explain her reasoning.

Folks often wonder about how much money Survivor contestants make, but in any given season there are number of other mysteries. Some fans have been wondering why Kristin let her grubs go free instead of having a chance at winning the Merge Feast, and over on her Instagram she offered some context. In a video she said:

I've studied a lot for a lot of aspects of Survivor and I know where my blindspots are. And one of them is the gross food challenge. I'm a vegetarian, so when you put something in front of me that's alive, that's next level.

I knew it. There was something about Kristin's crunchy vibe that signaled vegetarian to me. While she might have had some meat on a reward or while starving in Fiji, the act of eating a living creature was a step too far. So why compromise her morality when she might still end up losing the challenge and not even getting the merge feast?

Later in her same Instagram video, Kristin spoke more about what was going on in her mind when she decided to opt out of the gross food challenge on Survivor 51. In her words:

So when I saw these guys sitting on this plate in front of me, trying to get away, I was like 'I'm not sure I'm gonna be able to do this, but let's think it through' I looked at the side of the plate, it was pretty sharp and I thought 'I could cut their heads off and then try to get them down.' And while I was making that plan I thought 'Wow. It is very unlikely that I'm going to pull this thing off.' So why would I kill creatures in a game of charcuterie that I wasn't gonna win?

Honestly, this makes a ton of sense. Eating something nasty is one thing, but it was another for Flickinger to kill a living creature. What's more, she might not be starving as much as other Survivor players; she was shown having a real understanding about what Fijian wildlife could be used as food. The Merge Feast also ended up being a glorified charcuterie, so I have to assume she wouldn't have eaten any of the cured meets that Brady and others were chowing dow on.

I assumed that Kristin's vegetarianism was at the heart of the matter, some fans were criticizing her decision to opt out of eating the grubs. Some responses from Twitter include:

To be fair, the grubs weren't part of an actual immunity challenge. That might have motivated Kristin to give it a try, but in the end she was merely competing for one food reward. So it wasn't worth it to sacrifice her morals, especially with the two grubs alive and crawling around on her plate.

While she's gotten some hate online for this decision, Survivor fans have also immortalized Kristin's decision through some solid memes. You can check one out below:

Kristin with her plate of grubs: #Survivor #Survivor51 https://t.co/qxaQKsqYKVNovember 5, 2026

Survivor fans are known for being passionate, and often make the most memorable moment of each new episode into A+ memes. There were a bunch about Kristin refusing to eat the grubs, to hilarious results. We'll just have to wait and see what comes out of the next episode of the Emmy-winning competition series.

Survivor airs new episodes Wednesdays as part of the 2026 TV schedule. Kristin is still arguably my favorite player of the season, so fingers crossed she makes it deep into the game.

#3704. Report: James Gunn Ousted Amid Messy Power Struggle Despite Superman’s Success

ClayfaceDC StudiosJames GunnPeter SafranSupergirlSuperman

Yesterday, James Gunn and Peter Safran stepped down from their positions as co-presidents at DC Studios. This was after just four years on the job and only three movies in the new superhero cinematic universe they were overseeing. The pair has now been replaced by ex-Marvel producer Jeremy Latcham, whose evangelical history has given some DC fans pause. So what happened? According to a new report by The Hollywood Reporter, trouble had been brewing for the pair as soon as the Skydance merger went through earlier this year.

According to THR‘s sources, on Friday, November 6, Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz informed the pair that, despite previously being told they would be part of the company moving forward, there had been a “change of plans.” The shake-up had reportedly been in the works since “early fall,” with Latcham having been contacted about potentially taking over DC Studios by Skydance Motion Picture Group co-chair John Greenstein, who worked with Latcham during his time at Marvel.

THR says that there were multiple points of “tension” between Gunn and Safran on one hand and the Skydance execs on the other. Gunn and Safran initially reported directly to Warner Bros. CEO David Zaslav, and their contracts said they would maintain that kind of direct reporting structure even in the event of a change in leadership, so they would have reported to Ellison following the merger. Meanwhile, Greenstein and co-chair Dana Goldberg were reportedly trying to consolidate movie production under their leadership, while Gunn and Safran had grown “accustomed to having strong control” over anything under the DC Studios banner.

Other points of contention included that Gunn and Safran were reportedly âslowâ and “not forthcoming” in sharing plans and footage with the Skydance leads.

Many will point to Supergirl‘s box office bomb as a sticking point, and I’ve even seen a lot of people joke that Gunn and Safran only got “one bad movie” before they were thrown out. While Supergirl‘s performance is noted as a problem by THR‘s sources, apparently even their biggest hit, Superman, wasn’t doing enough in the eyes of their corporate overlords. That film, which grossed $618 million on a $225 budget, “did not net out, or have the kind of pop culture impact, in the way that kind of movie should,” in the eyes of Skydance.

Sources say that Gunn is “somewhat relieved” to be out of the business side of things and now focusing on filmmaking. His DC next film, Man of Tomorrow, is set to premiere next year.

As for Latcham, THR‘s sources call him a “down-the-middle shooter” who is more concerned with making “hits for the masses” than Gunn, whose projects often feature somewhat profane writing and obscure characters.

Clayface, the last DC Studios project produced while Gunn and Safran were company co-presidents, is in theaters now.

#3702. Switch 2 and Switch consoles updated to version 23.5.0 as Nintendo quietly re-introduces eShop gifting

Nintendo has just pushed out a new update to all Switch and Switch 2 consoles, bringing the firmware on both up to version 23.5.0. The headline change with the new update is support and compatibility for an upcoming update that will allow members of a Nintendo Account family group to gift games to one another.

The feature itself is expected to go live on 17th November, 2026. "Just in time for the holidays, a new feature will let family group members gift digital games to other members of their group," says a post on a dedicated blog on the Nintendo site. "You will be able to gift digital products that you purchase through Nintendo eShop on your device to family group members. This includes eligible games as well as DLC and upgrade packs. As a reminder, anyone with a Nintendo Account can easily set up a family group and add members (up to 8 total)."

The publisher notes, however, that "some products may not be eligible for digital gifting" and that "supervised accounts are not able to send digital gifts". Additionally, "the number of digital gift purchases allowed in a given period is limited".

"This feature is a great way to celebrate a special occasion with your kids. Happy gifting!" concludes Nintendo. Just in time for the holidays, how thoughtful. It's worth noting that a previous iteration of this support was included back on the Nintendo Wii, but that was much more robust than this - back then, the publisher allowed users to send WiiWare or Virtual Console games to anyone on their Wii Friend list via the Wii Shop Channel, rather than just those limited to their immediate group. This functionality was lost in 2019, alongside the closure of the Wii Shop Channel.

Could a remade Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time be exciting enough to revitalise Switch 2 hardware sales? That was the big question. And early sales figures suggest the answer is yes, it can.

The Switch 2, which had been declining in hardware sales over the last few months, just had its highest (dollar) sales week of 2026 in the US so far following the game's release, according to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella on Bluesky.

The accompanying Legend of Zelda: 40th Anniversary Edition console in particular is responsible for a notable jump in Switch 2 hardware dollar sales. The themed, special edition console has been popular, with various retailers immediately running out of stock and a rise in scalping.

It's worth noting that The Legend of Zelda: 40th Anniversary Edition console, priced $520 / £430, does not include a copy of the game. Also, because the console was released 29th October, and the Ocarina of Time remake on 5th November, their sales results will come in separate monthly reports.

The Ocarina of Time launch also caused US hardware spending to jump by 81 percent during the week ending 31st October compared to the same period last year.

Christian Donlan awarded The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time a glitzy five stars in Eurogamer's review, writing: "This is Ocarina as it's always been, as timeless and intricate, but it also has a vibrancy and clarity that makes it feel like it was just created last Wednesday."

#3699. Rockstar Says GTA VI Is ‘Targeting’ 30 FPS And Will Use PSSR On PS5 Pro

If you pre-ordered a digital version of GTA VI, you can preload it right now, and considering its massive file-size, getting a nine-day head start on that download might be a good idea. But in addition to announcing the pre-load, Rockstar Games has revealed some extra information on the game’s specifications and features, and a brief but glittery new trailer to accompany the announcement.

The biggest thing on the list of specifications is the framerate. Sorry to anyone hoping for a buttery-smooth 60 FPS on console but GTA VI, according to Rockstar, is “targeting 30 frames per second.” That word “targeting” seems especially fraught, suggesting you might not even get all 30 frames all the time.

On the PS5 Pro the game will make use of PSSR upscaling and feature ray-tracing while your regular degular PS5 consoles get “high-fidelity haptic feedback fully integrated across the game on DualSense controllers and adjustable via accessibility settings, improved spatial audio rendering […], and improved load times.”

Over on the Xbox side of things, you’ll be able to play the game via Xbox Cloud Streaming on the X and S console, and on the Xbox One with Series S graphics. Rockstar warns that trying to stream the game might lead to some technical difficulties. “Connection speeds and other technical factors may influence game performance in ways that would not impact local gameplay,” Rockstar’s announcement reads. “GTAVI will also fully support Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox.”

It is not long now, and with this new information, GTA VI feels even closer.

Sony took another step back from the PC today, announcing that the PlayStation Plus app for PC will be "retiring" on December 10. I can't really blame it for this one, though: Almost nobody was actually using it.

"PlayStation believes in providing high-quality experiences to our players, and we regularly review offerings to ensure we are focusing on experiences our members value most," Sony wrote at the tail-end of a PlayStation Blog update detailing the PlayStation Plus game lineup for November.

"With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4%) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use. As a result, the PlayStation Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available."

The end of the app seems to fit pretty well with Sony's recent about-face on PC gaming: After a brief period of enthusiasm for bringing its big exclusives to PC, Sony began a walkback earlier this year, shifting its focus back to consoles exclusives. It hasn't explicitly acknowledged or explained the change in strategy, but as PC Gamer's Morgan Park wrote in May, the thing speaks for itself: Rather like Xbox "recommitting" to its console, "Sony is responding to a waning interest in consoles by reinforcing its 'narrative singleplayer games' as system sellers once again.

"Multiplayer games like the upcoming Marvel Tōkon will still come to PC, but if you want to play the next prestige action game from the likes of Naughty Dog or Insomniac, you'll need a PS5," Morgan wrote. Or, when the time comes, a PlayStation 6.

Similar to Xbox cloud streaming, the PlayStation Plus app on PC was really more noteworthy for the selection of older PlayStation games it offered to PC gamers, rather than major new releases. Given that, I think the end has come for exactly the reason Sony cited: Not due to any strategic realignment, but simply because nobody's using it in the first place.

#3697. Under pressure, Big Walk studio reveals it used generative AI "sparingly" while making its hit 2026 game

"It has become a matter of public interest."

Australian developer House House has revealed it used generative AI "sparingly" to help make celebrated, indie, multiplayer puzzle game Big Walk.

In a statement sent to Aftermath - following a judging fallout related to the Independent Games Festival - House House revealed it had used large language models primarily to help debug the game's code.

"In the final stretch of Big Walk's development, LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs," the developer said. "In some cases, snippets from LLM responses were copied as a starting point to be modified into game code - we'd estimate that well under 0.1 percent of Big Walk's code had anything to do with this usage, and generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game."

House House added: "The primary use case for House House's use of LLMs was to research, via chatbots, issues we encountered with third-party code."

The studio's revelation comes after a sizeable number of IGF jurors - 19 of them - issued a statement saying they would not vote for any game that used generative AI during its development. This was done after seeing "a significant increase" in entry submissions involving generative AI use, which "set off some fairly intense discussion and disagreement across the judge and jury pools". And rather than not vote for these in silence, a collection of jurors decided to take a public stand.

House House hadn't disclosed Big Walk generative AI use anywhere before disclosing it for its IGF submission. "We have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage," the studio explained. "We are posting this disclosure as it has become a matter of public interest."

House House added: "This is not an endorsement of, or argument for, the use of AI tools, however minimal. We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as 'inevitable'. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to video games and our world, and apologise that Big Walk's LLM usage may not meet their standards.

"Big Walk was developed without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards."

It's a revelation that's likely to leave a taint of some degree on one of this year's brightest stars - a game Eurogamer awarded a full five stars to in its Big Walk review.

#3695. Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Has A Massive Second-Act Change That Took My Breath Away

Nintendo Switch 2The Legend of ZeldaThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

Last night in my playthrough of Ocarina of Time, I finished up the Fire Temple and headed (as one does) to Zora Domain, expecting it to be (as the rest of the game has been so far) very much like the original in structure, just visually more elaborate. And it was, mostly. But as I passed through the realm, I also encountered one of my favorite new additions to the remake so far, one that simultaneously clears up one of Ocarina of Time‘s long-enduring inconsistencies, while also adding pretty significant elements of both horror and hope to the original story.

In the original Ocarina of Time, Zora Domain in the adult timeline is completely frozen over. When Link enters, there are no Zora to be foundâjust an iced-over pond and a frozen waterfall. At the top, you can find King Zora, encased in red ice. Through your adventures in Ice Cavern and later Water Temple, you learn that Ganondorf is (of course) responsible, and that all the Zora have been completely frozen. Sheik was able to save Ruto, who goes on to become the Sage of Water, and you’re later able to thaw out King Zora using Blue Fire.

But the fate of the rest of the Zora is sort of…ambiguous. Presumably due to technical limitations in the original, Zora Domain in adult timeline remains frozen over even post-Water Temple, and the Zora people are nowhere to be found. It’s just King Zora, sitting on his icy throne, for the rest of the game, and Ruto now effectively dead to the world in the Sacred Realm as a sage. You do see some Zora in the credits sequence at the end of the game, implying that some survived, but just what happened to Hyrule’s aquatic folk more broadly remains pretty murky.

The remake clears that up, but the way it does this made me say “holy shit”Â out loud several times.

When you enter Zora Domain as adult Link, you’re treated to a souped-up version of the same sight: frozen pond, frozen waterfall, frozen everything. New to the remake is a haunting new piece of music that does a great job of conveying the frozen emptiness you’re faced with. I hate that you can occasionally hear snippets of the main Zora theme instruments creeping in between the weird, spooky noises! Agh!

But even worse (read: better) than this is what you see when you go out onto the pond. And look down. Into the ice.

Uh, yeah. That’s what that is. That’s where they are. They are actively frozen beneath their own pond. You can just. See them. Down there. Trapped. Dead? Effectively tortured by cold?! Holy shit.

I haven’t finished the Water Temple yet. I considered waiting until I had finished it to write this blog, but I decided to write it now because I wanted to talk about the other emotion, aside from horror, that seeing this inspired. If the Zora are in there now, that opens the door for them to be freed when I finish Water Temple. There are no technical limitations prohibiting Nintendo from thawing out Zora Domain when the time comes and giving these people their lives back. Can Ruto and I really, truly, conclusively save the Zora this time around?

Right now, I am loving the anticipation! I can’t wait to finish the Water Temple tonight, and while I’m a little afraid of being disappointed by the outcome in case Nintendo decided to leave the Zora in this horrible frozen state until the credits, the overall excellence and attention to detail of the Ocarina of Time remake so far has given me ample reason for hope.

Perhaps the most startling moment in a movie filled with WTF moments is when Amanda Seyfried suddenly appears in You Can See Everything. The star of the Elizabeth Holmes series The Dropout, which you can watch with a Hulu subscription, shows up about halfway through the documentary. First, just as herself, then later reprising her role from The Dropout as Holmes. It became a code among those who made the movie, and later those who saw it, to keep this reveal a secret, and that included, most of all, Seyfried herself.

It’s created some awkward moments for the Emmy winner on red carpets lately. Those moments started well before the movie was widely released and were seen by only a handful of festivalgoers at the Telluride Film Festival. However, once the movie was screened, some outlets did let slip the secret that Seyfried had a big role in it. That’s when the awkwardness began.

Take, for example, an exchange just a week or so after the film screened at Telluride. Seyfried, attending a premiere for another movie at the Toronto Film Festival, is asked by Entertainment Tonight if she’s going to be “part of the new Elizabeth Holmes documentary.” Her response is a masterclass in dodging the question, evoking her Dropout colleagues:

Everybody who's asking me about it, like, so many people from The Dropout keep texting me about it. It's Nathan Fielder, and I know what he does. It's wild, and everybody is saying that it's wild. So I don't know. I want to know more about it!

She doesn’t deny being in the movie, nor does she confirm. There are politicians on Capitol Hill who aren’t this deft at ignoring a question they don’t want to answer, but still say something interesting. Keeping the secret was crucial for the movie, and really, for the viral marketing of the film. Word of mouth has carried this documentary to box office heights that very few docs ever come close to approaching. That’s in large part due to word of mouth, including people telling their friends things like, “You won’t believe the twist!”

You Can See Everything is being talked about for a lot of possible Oscar nominations, including Seyfried for Best Supporting Actress. That would be another unprecedented achievement for a documentary, and I still think it’s a longer shot than other awards watchers, but it’s not out of the question. For the record, I’m rooting for it to happen.

Seyfried deserves the accolades not only for her performance and for the question-dodging skills she’s employed so often over the last couple of months when asked about her secret role in one of the season’s biggest hits.

If you're a World of Warcraft: Forever player you're almost certainly having your free time drained as you chain yourself to your desktop PC to play the game, or maybe a laptop. But for a small selection of true enthusiasts, the game is already working on mobile and handheld devices.

One such person showing off WoW: Forever on the go is none other than director of publishing at Larian, Michael Douse, who took to Twitter to show off the MMO being played on an AYN Thor device. For those who don't know, this is a fancy android handheld console, a sort of beefed up DS for the modern handheld aficionado.

"Arguably too many layers of abstraction," writes Douse. In the picture he posted, you can see the player character viewable on the Thor's top screen, while the map, text chat, skill UI, and buffs viewable on the bottom. It looks pretty cool, and is made possible due to JReese702's Github mod you can download at your leisure.

Arguably too many layers of abstraction pic.twitter.com/VjW0IX00Gg

But it's not the only mo-bell at the ball. Another Github WoW: Forever mod, WolkaraForever, gets the game playable on the iPhone Duo. As highlighted by CEO of esports company 100 Thieves Alex Wechsler on Twitter, the game looks to be ported pretty well to the phone, with mobile touchscreen controls viewable on both sides of the screen. Be warned though, as confirmed by Wechsler in a Twitter reply, it'll get your phone running hot.

As a father of 2 kids and always having wanted to play WOW, I’ve finally found a way 🥹 pic.twitter.com/eIVn0gn1WC

This coming alongside World of Warcraft: Forever's built-in (and very good) controller support could mean the game has real potential to spread far and wide across the vast array of different hardware out there. Blizzard has already hinted at plans of porting the game to other platforms, so who knows? Maybe we can expect an official mobile port to tread the path paved by these community-made mods.

#3691. As Arc Raiders celebrates its first birthday, publisher Nexon reveals the extraction shooter has topped 17 million sales, but revenue is set to decline

Arc Raiders, Embark Studios' popular extraction shooter, has exceeded 17m copies sold, according to publisher Nexon.

Arc Raiders was released at the end of October 2025, so reaching that milestone in a year is nothing to scoff at. According to Nexon's latest earnings report, however, only 1m copies of those 17 were sold in the third quarter - meaning sales have certainly slowed down.

Relatedly, Nexon said it expects Arc Raiders' revenue to decline in the fourth quarter compared to the same period last year - when the game enjoyed its hugely successful launch - and anticipates revenue will be "broadly flat sequentially". Despite this, the company said Arc Raiders' revenue was "within the outlook", naming its Frozen Trail update as a key moment that brought back some lapsed players while introducing new ones.

Indeed, Frozen Trail boosted the game's Steam player count, and reports suggest it also helped Arc Raiders hit a six-month player high across various platforms.

Even with its slowing sales, Arc Raiders remains one of Nexon's most successful titles. The company primarily attributed an overall year-on-year revenue increase, for the nine months ended 30th September, to the game.

Looking ahead, the biggest question hanging over Arc Raiders is whether or not it's going to get a dedicated PvE playlist. Following a successful test earlier this summer, Embark has been coy, and hasn't said whether PvE will return as a permanent feature. Arc Raiders' Chinese version does have a dedicated PvE mode, and executive producer Aleksander Grøndal said he could see both PvP and PvE modes co-existing in the future.

#3689. Where to catch Bloodgill in DREADMOOR

While attempting to fix all tuning forks in DREADMOOR, Malcolm will meet the enigmatic Father Matthias, who will task him with catching two Bloodgill fish if he wants to finish his quest.

The fish’s location, however, won’t be marked on your map, making it a matter of knowing where to search. To help you save both fuel and time, here’s where to catch Bloodgill in DREADMOOR, as well as what you must do after giving them to Father Matthias.

Contrary to what you might imagine, you won’t be able to find Bloodgill spawns close to Father Matthias’ island in DREADMOOR. Instead, you can catch the fish by heading to the spot marked below, located south of The Slough’s Trading Post. The fish will become way more common after you reach the Big Hollow, though, and will be easy to spot close to the post’s new location.

Like all other predatory catches, the Bloodgill can be angled with both the Rainbow Fin and Flaming Belly baits. You can check out the items needed to craft both below, as well as get the Flaming Belly recipe by purchasing it from Gill and Bozur for 80 Coins at the trading post. To see how to unlock all other baits, take a look at our How to get all bait recipes in DREADMOOR guide.

After giving the fish to Father Matthias, you can then progress through the quest by heading to the top of the island and placing both the tuning fork prongs and the other required items at its ritual site. Make sure to also sleep before heading back to the trading post to avoid the dangers of nighttime.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Two years after the release of Unknown 9: Awakening, its one and only game, Bandai Namco's Reflector Entertainment is closing.

The shutdown was revealed in a notice posted by Banda Namco (via Game Informer) saying the company "has passed a resolution to dissolve and liquidate its consolidated subsidiary Reflector Entertainment." The decision was made "after comprehensively considering future business plans, necessary additional investment, and the possibility of profitability and business continuation," Bandai Namco said.

Unknown 9: Awakening, featuring The Witcher star Anya Chalotra as a woman able to travel into a mysterious dimension known as the Fold, showed potential in our pre-release preview as a "linear, narrative-driven, set-piece laden" game drawing from Xbox 360 releases of the late 2000s.

The full game, however, landed with a thud. A month after launch, Reflector laid off 18% of its workforce; a few months after that, in January 2025, more layoffs followed as an in-development project was cancelled. Reflector CEO Herve Hoerdt said at the time that the decision "correlates directly with the failure of the studio's ambitious and courageous first project [Unknown 9: Awakening]," which "didn't come near the company expectations."

Reflector confirmed the coming end of operations in its own message on LinkedIn, writing that "after reviewing the progress of our latest project in pre-production, future development requirements, and current market conditions, Bandai Namco concluded that it could not justify several more years of investment."

Bandai Namco said the liquidation of Reflector Entertainment is expected to happen "once the necessary procedures according to local laws are completed," but a concrete schedule has not been set.

#3687. Steam now shows average Steam Deck framerates when browsing games, but Valve says it's considering expanding the feature to other hardware

By providing average data for each game, customers now have a more complete picture".

Valve has released a new Steam update that adds Steam Deck framerate data to a game's store page, giving potential buyers an indication of how well a game runs on the handheld.

As per Valve's announcement post, average framerates are now listed in the Steam Deck Compatibility section of a game's store page, but you'll need to click Learn More to see it. Additionally, the feature is only available for games that have been tested for Deck compatibility - those with Verified, Playable, or Unsupported badges - so while it's not a complete list, it still covers thousands of titles.

According to Valve, average framerates are derived from players running the game on their Steam Decks, assuming they've opted in to provide framerate data. And the store widget also includes another helpful addition: a histogram displaying the percentage of data samples. This shows how often a particular framerate has been reported, and is useful in determining if the game's framerate is sporadic, such as due to stutters.

"The current Steam Deck Verified compatibility rating is based on standardised test criteria, but it may not match every customer's bar for acceptable gameplay," Valve explained of the new feature.

"This is especially true around performance - a game with an Unsupported rating due to unstable performance may be considered playable by some customers, and a Verified game may not reach a framerate that some customers prefer to play at. By providing average framerate data for each game, customers now have a more complete picture of how the game performs on Steam Deck and can make more informed purchase and play decisions."

Currently, Steam's framerate data feature only covers performance on Steam Deck, and for a very good reason: Valve's handheld has standardised hardware, so the results will be the same for all players. However, Valve says it intends to provide framerate data for more devices in the future, but it's not clear if that's ever going to include desktop PCs, considering the complex nature of their hardware configurations.

#3686. Remember PS5-exclusive shooter Fairgame$? It’s reportedly canceled now, to no one’s surprise

Well, it seems like this one was only a matter of time.

Sony has reportedly canceled the long-missing online shooter Fairgame$ after it went missing in the public eye for years, according to Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier, adding to a long list of canceled PlayStation projects this generation.

Schreier said that “a recent test of the game with thousands of players did not deliver on the results PlayStation expected,” according to an internal email sent to employees today.

First revealed at PlayStation Showcase way back in May 2023, the game seemed to be themed around online heist PvP gameplay. But it hasn’t been seen since, and this cancellation comes as little surprise, as rumors about turmoil in development have been swirling for some time.

“While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” executives Sean Decker and John Doyle said in the memo. “Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.”

Earlier this year, it was reported that Fairgame$ was pivoting away from the “heist” mechanic and instead focusing on the extraction game type, similar to Bungie’s Marathon and Call of Duty’s DMZ. It apparently did not work out.

Fairgame$, developed by Haven Studios, joins a long list of PS5 projects that did not make the cut this generation as Sony incessantly chased live-service success. Concord launched and was quickly shuttered, while The Last of Us Factions, a God of War game, a Spider-Man game, Twisted Metal, and more never saw the light of day from PS5’s games-as-a-service initiative.

According to Schreier, “there will be no job cuts as a result of the cancellation,” and “Haven will instead move to support other studios within the organization.”

While Donald Trump and the White House have engaged in verbal back-and-forths with several late-night talk show hosts, the bulk of those have arguably been with Jimmy Kimmel. The Live! star has notably taken multiple shots at POTUS over the years and received blistering responses as a result. In more than a few of those cases, Kimmel has directly addressed the sentiments shared by Trump and co. on air. And, just recently, Kimmel responded to the assertion that he supposedly has a “peanut-sized brain.”

It’s during Jimmy Kimmel Live!’s opening monologues that viewers typically hear the titular host’s thoughts on President Trump and other political matters. During the November 9 broadcast that aired amid the 2026 TV schedule, Kimmel discussed a statement that was recently released by White House spokesperson Davis Dingle. As can be seen on YouTube, Kimmel laid out the message, which not only included comments about his intelligence but also took aim at his skills as a host and more:

Then the White House got back to the important business of attacking me. I got another statement from White House spokesboy Davis Dingle, who wrote, ‘Jimmy Kimmel’s case of Trump Derangement Syndrome is so advanced that it has completely rotted his peanut-sized brain. He’s far more entertaining when you’re laughing at him than with him. But unfortunately, his real talent is his failing ratings.

Just weeks ago, Dingle chastised Kimmel via another statement and, at that point, he declared that the media personality was “so devoid of actual talent that nobody with any common sense would ever watch him unless it was to laugh at his miserable failures.” And, days prior, President Trump insulted Kimmel as well, calling him a “loser” after the host made jokes about the attendance level at his recent rallies. Kimmel responded with quips while recapping those situations on air, and he did the same thing this time around.

Ultimately, Kimmel didn’t seem too fazed by the sentiments shared by Dingle. With that, he proceeded to share a jokey pitch to the White House employee:

Sick burn, bro. You know what? You should enter a rap battle spitting dope rhymes like that.

Kimmel didn’t finish there, as he also mused that “Trump now has interns insulting me.” As of this writing, the WH hasn’t responded to that “rap battle” comment. Overall, though, this marks just another chapter in the Kimmel/White House/Trump saga. The verbal skirmishes have become so notable at this point that fellow late-night TV hosts Seth Meyers and John Oliver have joked that Trump hates Kimmel the most amongst them and their peers. Kimmel hasn’t just dropped jokes when discussing the current administration, though.

At this point, Kimmel is of the belief that the late-night TV world is “being poisoned” in part due to this political landscape. Months ago, he was also asked what he believed would help save the format, and Kimmel got political by saying, “A different president would be a good start.” On that note, President Trump still has two more years in office, and it remains to be seen what kind of barbs his administration will trade with Kimmel moving forward.

Jimmy Kimmel Live! airs weeknights at 11:35 p.m. ET on ABC.

#3683. Rockstar kills any hopes of streaming GTA 6 from Xbox to PC, but you can stream it to your old Xbox One if you like

Rockstar Games has today clarified a few remaining details about Grand Theft Auto 6's framerate target and visual settings on PlayStation 5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X/S. And as part of the same announcement, the developer revealed a key detail about the game's cloud streaming options.

GTA 6 will be available to stream via Xbox Cloud Gaming. However, this is only possible on Xbox Series X/S consoles, as well as - surprisingly - the last generation console, Xbox One. Notably, that means you can't use Xbox Cloud Gaming to stream to PC, or other devices, despite it being useable there.

You may recall that in early October, a Verge report said Microsoft had acquired exclusive cloud streaming rights for GTA 6, with the understanding being that the game would be available to stream on any XCloud-supported device - as in, to PC as well. Xbox immediately shot down the report, saying GTA 6 "will not be streaming exclusively or to PC".

Perhaps more surprisingly, the cloud-streamed version will be using Series S graphics settings, not those of the more powerful Series X console. Considering the loss in quality inherent in cloud streaming, this will make for a less-than-ideal way of experiencing the game.

Beyond cloud streaming, GTA 6 supports Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox, so you can stream the game on your local network to any device, from a PS5 or Xbox Series X/S console.

GTA 6 pre-loading is now available across PlayStation and Xbox. The code-in-box physical editions have also started shipping, letting you claim the code and pre-load your copy in time for GTA 6's 19th November launch.

#3682. How to gain more Followers in Warhammer Survivors

Gaining Followers in Warhammer Survivors has many benefits when it comes to the survival aspect of the game. Not only do they help you survive and last longer in the battle, but you’ll need to gain a minimum number if you want to complete the objectives.

While this method talks about gaining 5 followers, it can be any arbitrary number. I say 5 because that’s a requirement of an in-game objective that unlocks a crucial item. There is more than one way to gain followers, but this will be the easiest one for you.

First, unlock Trooper Bartosz Kozlowski and Sister Superior Amalia Novena, followed by their respective weapons. Now, begin a fresh run with Malum Caedo.

Once you’re deeper into your run, you’ll be offered the Lasgun and Shield of Faith as available weapons. Grab both of them, and then upgrade the Lasgun to Level 6. This will make Bartosz Kozlowski bring the required number of followers.

If you’re one short, that’s where Sister Amalia comes in. Once you acquire the Shield of Faith as a weapon, you’ll manage to have her as a companion. This will also unlock the Figure Case passive skill that allows you to return after dying.

You can repeat the same process with other characters in the game. Several characters allow you to add to the count of Followers when you unlock their signature weapon and level it up. However, the characters I have mentioned above are easy to unlock, and they will allow you to get to five Followers fast.

#3681. Europe is about to get very tough on loot boxes in games, according to a leaked draft of the landmark Digital Fairness Act

"The digital era has fundamentally transformed consumer experiences..."

An alleged draft of the potentially game-changing Digital Fairness Act has leaked ahead of its scheduled publication tomorrow (11th November), containing proposals that could dramatically affect the way games operate and are monetised within the European Union.

The draft, published by French publication Contexte (via Video Games Industry Memo) goes as far as to recommend that loot boxes (uncertainty-based rewards) be turned off by default for minors, as well as the sale of in-game items and currencies. There's also a recommendation that all players - not just minors - should be able to turn off offers related to these lootboxes and gambling mechanics.

"The digital era has fundamentally transformed consumer experiences," the draft of the Digital Fairness Act begins. "It has enabled faster, more convenient and wider access to an ever-increasing range of goods and services. At the same time, it has given rise to new and more sophisticated ways of influencing consumers' choices.

"Along with the indisputable benefits in choice and efficiency, the extensive use of digital technologies allows both old and new unfair commercial practices to affect consumers at scale, exacerbating risks to their economic interests, as well as to their mental and physical wellbeing. Vulnerable consumers are particularly affected."

The Digital Fairness Act calls for greater transparency around a "transactional decision". Which means: "Price transparency on the real value of in-app purchases using virtual currencies and the probabilities of winning for virtual offers with uncertainty-based rewards (loot boxes).

"All consumers can turn off virtual offers with uncertainty-based rewards. Some spending-maximising practices prohibited for minors, with the remaining turned off by default. Supporting self-regulation for video games and legal obligation for video games to have an age-appropriate rating. All consumers can turn off attention-maximising features, with some prohibited for minors and the remaining turned off by default."

"Spending-maximising" refers to systems that pressure us to spend more money than we want to, such as reward systems or pay-to-progress or pay-to-win systems. They're all being targeted here, as is virtual currency, which provides a layer of abstraction as to the real cost of goods.

"It may be difficult for minors to resist such perceived pressure to pay," the Digital Fairness Act said with regard to progression-linked systems. "Therefore, where a product is directed at minors or when the trader is aware with reasonable certainty that the product is used by minors, pay-to-progress or pay-to-win mechanisms [...] should not be made available to minors."

The Digital Fairness Act is a forthcoming European legislative proposal designed to update consumer protection rules for various digital dangers that we face today. Importantly, it's not law yet, and it has iterations and discussions to go through before it will be. A timeline on the Digital Fairness Act explainer website suggests it could be adopted late in 2027, then applied more broadly by 2030.

It's also hoping to tackle many things besides shady video game monetisation, including "problematic" influencer marketing, "unfair" pricing practices - such as obscuring the real cost of something until you've progressed through layers trying to buy it - and mysterious-sounding "dark patterns". These relate to 'easy to sign-up, hard-to-cancel' processes, it seems.

These changes aren't happening in a vacuum. Earlier this year, the well-known European age-rating body PEGI announced historic alterations to its game-rating criteria, with an eye to better categorising the dangers of loot box-containing games and aggressively monetised games. These changes have already started to roll out and mean that a game like EA Sports FC, which was previously routinely rated PEGI 3, now automatically gets a PEGI 16 rating because of its Ultimate Team card pack (loot box) system.

The effect of the Digital Fairness Act could tip the balance against these systems being included in games at all. Expect more discussion and digestion of the proposed changes as the Act is officially published tomorrow.

#3680. A Big Talk About Big Walk’s AI Fallout

Big Walk, the game that was likely at or near the top of a lot of people’s game of the year lists, was made in very small part with the use of AI. This was not previously disclosed publicly or on Steam because, according to House House’s statement on the matter, “the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage.” And we’re only finding out about this now, long after the game has released to universal acclaim, because Big Walk was apparently at the heart of a fractious discussion about AI usage in development and the game’s eligibility for awards among the jury members for the 2027 Independent Games Festival.

Over the past month, IGF judges and jurists have had intense, difficulty, generous, and deeply engaged conversations about AI and the games industry.

This statement is the result of those conversations.

— austin_walker (@austinwalker.bsky.social) 2026-11-09T22:42:15.552Z

Some jurors felt that a hard, no-exceptions line needed to be drawn in the sand, and made a public, signed statement to that effect. Others felt that considering how House House used the tech was worth consideration in determining Big Walk‘s eligibility. House House claims that “well under 0.1% of Big Walkâs code had anything to do with this usage and generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game,” and it seems like some jurors felt that such limited use shouldn’t disqualify a game that was very likely in the running for the Seumas McNally Grand Prize, the IGF’s top award.

The discussions about this event at Kotaku mirror those playing out amongst gamers and developers on social media. But at the heart of it all, this sucks man.

Ash: I have not played the game because I havenât taken the time to round up friends to play it with. It was important that I make an effort to try because this game seems so special to everyone Iâve seen talk about it. This whole thing, not just how AI was used but how we found out about it, definitely removes that urgency. Rebekah: I am not naive enough to believe that every game I play has zero AI touching it in any way. In fact, I assume many of them do. But I, and I think many others, made an assumption that based on the past stances of this dev team and their general attention to a lot of hand-crafted detail, AI would not even be a factor.Â

Carolyn Petit: I’m actually playing it right now with friends and it was certainly strange to emerge from our play session last night (for those whoâve played it, we just got the ski lift working!) and into the online discourse. My feeling is that the goal should be an expectation of zero AI usage on any level. It’s stolen labor no matter how you cut it. Does that mean I think House House should be crucified in the court of public opinion? Maybe not, but I do think we need to be clear about establishing and holding to that expectation moving forward, and I donât think it should receive honors at IGF. John Walker: I think itâs really important to recognize that of all the games weâve loved this year, almost all of them will have used LLMs as part of the coding process. I hate that, and I wish they had not, and I appeal to developers to stop doing it. But of all of the games to do this, I suspect Big Walk did it about the very least. Carolyn: Yes. I also think the statement from some jury members was great. And I don’t think we can ignore that this one hurts more than some disposable top-to-bottom AI slop on Steam because of how well-received Big Walk is and because of the dev teamâs commendable stance on things like BDS.

Not to say we should throw our hands in the air and give up, I just donât know where to begin pressuring major companies. Boycotts famously are not meaningfully impactful at the AAA level. I would really like to see people organize around finding solutions to that. Ash: I think it means getting a developer like House House to say âBecause of this, weâre gonna use Godot going forward.â Which I understand is incredibly easy for a non-developer to say. But we gotta coalition-build here. And having these arguments might be a baby step toward something like that.

Rebekah: It does. I want to encourage folks to participate in these conversations at the community level and find ways to organize around it and affect change within their groups, whether thatâs devs, consumers, media, whatever. Arguing on social media about it is cathartic but ultimately not super helpful. And also I certainly think reaching out to House House directly (and politely!) via official channels to tell them why this was hurtful will make a difference.

Ash: I think they know pretty well at this point. Rebekah: Sure, but again I think thereâs a difference between a lot of people yelling on social media and emailing them for comment, and someone who loved their game emailing them to tell them how this personally affects them

John: I was in a room with many indie developers on Saturday, and this discussion was had, and people calmly but passionately explaining why they refuse to use any AI at all was really affecting, and clearly influencing others who might âcompromiseâ here and there.

Ash: Coalition building! Seems maybe silly to ask, but is this game still your GOTY Rebekah? Carolyn? John? John: Iâm afraid, as a misanthrope, Iâve not played it. Carolyn: Iâm just playing it now. It was definitely shaping up to be on my list (probably not at the top but on the list somewhere), but now Iâll have to give it some thought. Rebekah: I honestly donât know what to do about it. It certainly calls into question whether the idea of âGOTYâ describes some sort of award or honor I am conferring on something for excellence, or if it just describes the best thing I played this year.

I cannot deny that it remains the best thing I played this year. The best experience I had. Iâd be lying to myself and everyone else to pretend it wasnât. But I also am not going to sit here and say this hasnât changed how I now look back on that experience, nor do I feel comfortable showing up to a Kotaku GOTY discussion to loudly go to bat for it as something deserving of a website-wide honor. Then again, how many other things that weâll argue for this year used AI in their development, and we donât know about it?

Where I sit right now is that I will probably pitch a piece solely on Big Walk for end-of-year discussions talking both about what it meant to me and why it was the best thing I played, and also how thatâs changed now. But as it stands I donât want to fight for it to win something thatâs seen as an âaward.â My feelings may change in either direction in the next few weeks. This is still pretty fresh. Ash: I still want to play it with yâall though, I think itâs worth at least that.

#3679. How to get the crude lockpick recipe in DREADMOOR, all lockpick types, and how to use them

Although brute force can take you far in DREADMOOR, having a lockpick at hand is a requirement if you wish to get past locked doors and access treasure chests across the game’s many settlements.

But getting the tool means first acquiring its recipe, something only doable a few hours in. Here’s how to get the first lockpick recipe in DREADMOOR and how the mechanic works.

You can unlock the Crude Lockpick recipe in DREADMOOR as a reward by completing the Catch a Mutant Fish Story Quest. The quest is unlocked after meeting Mad Nick on his island and requires catching two Cryptmaw fish.

The fish can be found in the locations below, but only late at night. You will also need to have at least 30 Line Strength to attempt the catch, so don’t forget to equip the Braided Line to your fishing rod at the trading post to meet the requirements.

After returning to Mad Nick and unlocking the recipe, you will be able to craft the Crude Lockpick by using 1x Rubber and 1x Metal Plate. You can have a maximum of twelve in your inventory. Just don’t forget, they will share slots with First Aid Kits.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

You can pick locks in DREADMOOR by first using your mouse to position your lockpick and find the sweet spot within the lock, marked by a glowing light. Now, hold D to turn the lock while keeping the tool in the right position to unlock it. Forcing the lock will cause your lockpick to break.

Apart from the Crude Lockpick, you can unlock two other variants in DREADMOOR: the standard iron Lockpick and the Master Lockpick. Both are clear upgrades and can be crafted after unlocking their respective recipes.

We will be adding more to the above once we unlock the recipes for the advanced lockpicks. In the meantime, don’t forget to check out all Fishing Rods and how they work in DREADMOOR.

Bungie has served up our first proper look at Marathon's big Symbiosis update, which is set to go live on December 8 with a permanent PvE mode, plus an all-new Team Deathmatch mode and a social space called Limbo.

Symbiosis represents the start of "the evolution of Marathon," Bungie said, with "a plethora of updates and changes" to the game. First and foremost is the addition of Marathon's PvE mode, now permanent and with a new name, Expedition, that's described in the teaser as a "co-op PvE roguelite." Details beyond that haven't been revealed just yet, but Bungie called it "phase one" of the team's PvE plan, suggesting that it remains a work in progress.

Also notable in Symbiosis is the addition of Limbo, a "social space" where players can hang out without getting aired out (although there does appear to be a little area set aside for friendly shootin'), and its firing range, a handy way to test the game's guns without having to venture into its less friendly locales.

Speaking of which, the Perimeter map is being expanded with new points of interest and tunnels, and a new sword-wielding runner shell, Bishop, will debut with the update. For those who prefer the PvP life, the update will also kick off a beta for Marathon's Team Deathmatch mode.

Overall, Symbiosis looks to be a pretty big deal, and while today's tease is light on detail, the early reaction among players on Reddit and social media seems quite positive. Bishop is already racking up fans:

One other bit of good news: The rollout of Symbiosis on December 8 will also mark the start of an "open play week," during which the game will be fully free to play, including the new modes and content. If you dig it and decide to stick around (ie., buy the game), any progress and items earned will carry over.

#3677. Rockstar details Grand Theft Auto 6 PS5 Pro enhancements, but it'll still only run at 30FPS

Pushing consoles to "their absolute limits".

As Grand Theft Auto 6 preloads go live, developer Rockstar has detailed the enhancements coming to the PS5 Pro version of the game, confirming these won't include framerates above the 30 FPS its targeting for consoles.

Rockstar shared the news in a blog post released to announce that GTA 6 pre-loading is now available ahead of its release date on 19th November.

"Grand Theft Auto 6 has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles," Rockstar says. It goes on to reconfirm GTA 6 is targeting 30 FPS on all consoles, saying the game is pushing modern machines "to their absolute limits" in order to "bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life — while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants."

PS5 players can expect high-fidelity haptic feedback through the DualSense controllers, improved spatial audio, and Tempest 3D audio, while PS5 Pro enhancements come in the form of PSSR support and ray tracing shadows, which should make the game look especially fancy, plus improved load times. PlayStation players can also expect remote play support. As for the Xbox, the post clarified details on Xbox Cloud Gaming, which will allow the game to be streamed to Xbox consoles including the Xbox One. Notably, this won't work on PC.

Grand Theft Auto 6's 30 FPS target was previously confirmed by Rockstar back in August, but there was some uncertainty around a possible 60fps performance mode at the time. Still, those PS5 technical boons do a lot of work to improve the games it's applied to, which if nothing else should mean GTA 6 will be quite the looker.
