#3676. I think China just taught a lesson about AI that US audiences really should learn

And I'm not talking about Nvidia-related spycraft.

One of the wildest entertainment stories of the year was Niu Lai, a Chinese animated film that immediately became a laughing stock for its incredibly rudimentary animation and character models.

And even though taste is in the eye of the beholder, I find it very hard to believe anyone would like this at face value. “Why is something that looks worse than many Newgrounds animations from the early ’00s even showing in theaters?” You might ask, but it turns out Niu Lai was a family’s labor of love that lucked into a modest distribution. This crucial piece of information turned the tide and got people to see the film in droves, giving it a $9 million theatrical run on a pretty much non-existent budget.

And while one could argue that a lot of people only started to care about the film because they learned the story about its creation, well, that’s completely fair, because film is a vessel for connection.

Niu Lai‘s story becomes even more interesting when you realize China recently saw the release of Sanxingdui: Future Past, the country’s first fully AI movie release, which bombed hard. Sure, it could perhaps make a comeback, but it can’t count on its development tale to pull the heartstrings of moviegoers because its production, like any other AI production, amounts to that of a bunch of guys using a computer to type the plot of the movie they wanted to rip off.

A studio spent $1.5 million on the first-ever theatrical AI film, which ended up grossing 100.000 dollars. A very different outcome from that of the millions of LinkedIn users who claim to have only spent $100 on a Lord of the Rings ripoff too ludicrous to even imagine.

Westerners with only one photo in their profile and no background to speak of often claim China’s population shows way more openness to the prospects of an AI-led future than the people of the West, but that might, fortunately, be bunk.

Unfortunately, however, the theatrical run of Wildwood shows that the West might’ve become too desensitized even for the most amazing displays of true animation prowess of all time. Yes, despite being arguably the most impressive animated film I’ve ever witnessed, and also being the result of many intense years of loving work, Laika’s epic also failed to even recoup its budget. Honestly, I’d normally advise you against seeing the trailer, but if that’s what’ll earn it a few more ticket sales, then so be it:

On top of being as far from using AI as a movie can get, Wildwood is also the best-rated animated movie in a decade. As far as technique and spectacle go, it’s perfectly reasonable to call this the Avatar or even the Star Wars of stop-motion movies—and a work capable of going toe to toe with any live-action or traditional ( or CGI) animated film, but people just didn’t care, or didn’t know.

Yeah, the marketing team either didn’t have the resources, or didn’t do a great job. Still, the stellar reactions to Wildwood should’ve at least granted it a healthy word-of-mouth-fed growth, but it’s yet to pass the $70 million mark worldwide, a number that stops very short of the movie’s budget—and truth is, the real budget has never even been officially revealed, but that can only mean it’s that big. And, if you’ve seen the movie, you’ll know there’s no way Laika studio pulled this off with the $100 million budget that some people were floating around.

It’s great to see Niu Lai succeed while an AI-made film crashes and burns, but it’d have been even better if that beautiful event had also sent shockwaves that got people to watch more beautifully crafted stuff, because we might never get to see anything like Wildwood again. Even if that means we might also not be seeing many more AI-made movies, either.

#3675. Grand Theft Auto 6 becomes the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation Store history

Sony has just announced that Grand Theft Auto 6 has become "the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store". Note, it's not the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation history, just on its digital PlayStation Store.

The announcement, which comes as Sony prepares to ditch physical releases for an all-digital future, was made in a PlayStation Blog post confirming pre-loads for GTA 6 are now live.

"Grand Theft Auto 6 is now the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store," Sony wrote. "Given this unprecedented demand, we've joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start pre-loading the game nine days early, so they're ready to play on launch day.

"We strongly advise that everyone who is hoping to play on launch day to pre-load the game as soon as possible," the blog post added. So: consider yourselves advised.

GTA 6 becomes available as soon as your region's clock ticks over from midnight into 19th November, which, if you're in New Zealand, means you'll play the game before everyone else. If only there were a way to pretend you lived there...

Elsewhere in the blog post, Sony underlined some features coming specially to GTA 6 on PS5 and PS5 Pro. On Xbox, meanwhile, cloud streaming is supported, but not - sadly - to PC.

Last night, in a Take-Two financial earnings call, company leader Strauss Zelnick said pre-orders for GTA 6 are tracking "far above expectations" and that soon, "numbers will speak for themselves". Presumably because they will be gripped by an excited form of sentience. It's expected that GTA 6 could become the best-selling instalment in an already mega-selling series; Zelnick reckons GTA 6 will "set a new baseline" for Take-Two in terms of success.

Have you managed to resist pre-ordering it yet?

#3674. How To Get A Sleeping Bag In World Of Warcraft: Forever

World of WarcraftWorld of Warcraft: Forever

If you’ve been partying up with others in World of Warcraft: Forever, you’ve probably seen a weird sleeping bag item being used by your teammates. You may have even been encouraged to use it yourself, and gotten a little EXP boost for your trouble. Now, having snuggled up in the sleeping bag with four of your dungeoning buddies, maybe you want this nap device for yourself and your own leveling journey. I am here to tell you how to get it. The journey is not without pain and sacrifice.

The Cozy Sleeping Bag is an item first introduced in WoW‘s Season of Discovery. It has unlimited uses on a one-hour-long cooldown. When you use it (the cast takes 15 whole seconds), you place a sleeping bag on the ground. If you stand still on top of it, your character will lay down after a few seconds and take a nap. In this state, you’ll gain a stack of a buff once every minute up to three stacks, with each stack giving you a 1-percent bonus to EXP earned that lasts through death, for two hours. So in total, you spend a little over three minutes to receive a 3-percent bump to EXP gained for two hours. The best part is that you can share this with your party members, so one sleeping bag will give your whole group a buff if everyone takes a nap together.

That said, given how long it takes to obtain, it’s…kind of a worthless reward. You’ll spend about the same amount of time you save in leveling just running all over the place to obtain the bag in the first place. It’s not a toy, so it takes up a precious inventory slot, too. That said, you do also get a 12-slot bag from the questline, which feels truly luxurious early in the game. And you can use this as an opportunity to pick up a bunch of useful flight points you’ll be happy to have later. As Horde, I grabbed flight points at places like Grom’gol, Booty Bay, Tarren Mill, Sunrock Retreat, and Hammerfall. I also did the early steps of this quest simultaneously with getting the Night Watchman’s Torch, which helped “save time” (if you can call any bit of this time-saving).

You’ll need to be at least level 14 to start this quest. Be warned, you will end up running into high-level areas to finish this, and will probably die a lot in the process. My general tip for this is to stay on the main roads whenever you can, as monsters tend to avoid them. However, some areas (like Stranglethorn Vale) will have monsters that will aggro you from off the path, and other places you’ll run through are PvP zones, so you may have to improvise. Just don’t be deceived into thinking that cross-country hikes are the best idea.

The first two steps are the only ones that are different depending on whether you’re Alliance or Horde. Both factions will have to complete both steps, just in reverse order from one another.

Alliance will start in Westfall. For Horde, this is your step two, so be prepared to come back to this momentarily. In Westfall, head for coordinates 37, 50 (you can see coordinates in the top right corner under your minimap, no add-ons required). Alliance can easily reach here from Stormwind as part of their normal questing journey, but Horde have a rougher time. Take the zeppelin from Orgrimmar to Stranglethorn Vale, then go north from Grom’gol through Darkshore and turn west when you can to Westfall. Beware, because Stranglethorn is full of high-level monsters that will aggro you if you breathe within a mile of them, and Darkshore and Westfall are full of Alliance NPCs. You can also swim the shore from Grom’gol up to the Westfall beach, if you prefer.

You’re looking to get to the middle of the Alexston Farmstead just southeast of the Gold Coast Quarry. There are a bunch of harvester enemies running around that may make things difficult, but if you can get clear of them you can interact with a Nailed Plank in a burnt-out cart. Alliance will pick up “…and that note you found” and Horde will get “Stepping Stones.”

Horde, you’ll start with this next step. Alliance, this is your step two. This one is in the Barrens. You’re looking for a burnt watchtower, at coordinates 46, 74 or so. Horde can get here easily by flying to Camp Taurajo (or walking from Orgrimmar, Crossroads, or Thunder Bluff) and taking the main road through the Barrens south. For Alliance, it’s a rougher journey, but you can make it by heading south from Darkshore (which is reachable by boat from Stormwind), through Ashenvale, and then down south further into the Barrens. At the watchtower, Horde will pick up the quest “…and that note you found” and Alliance will get “Stepping Stones.” Horde will then need to follow the previous step to Westfall to get their next quest.

Once you have “Stepping Stones,” the path is the same for both factions.

“Stepping Stones” takes you to Stonetalon Mountains, which Horde can get to from The Barrens and Alliance can get to…well, also from The Barrens, which is probably where you are if you just did the previous quest. Alliance have a hub at Stonetalon Peak, and Horde have Sunrock Retreat, but both groups will need to go past Sunrock Retreat and find a little path up into the mountains that lies just to the north of the outpost.

Follow the path carefully upward until you reach a small campsite with a fire, and a Pocket Litter you can interact with on top of a box. Finishing this quest will get you a 12-slot bag (yes!) and will let you pick up the next step, “Scramble.”

“Scramble”‘s turn-in point isn’t far away at all, but before you go, try to interact with the campfire. There’s a weird little quest you can do here called “Rekindle” that will restart the fire with the tinderbox and wood you got from the last quest. However, this quest was bugged for me when I did it and I was unable to click on the campfire, and this seems like a common problem a lot of people are experiencing. It will likely be patched in the future, but if it’s bugged when you reach it, don’t sweat it. You’re genuinely not missing any rewards and it’s not necessary to get the sleeping bag.

Campfire or no, head due north and up the hill, walking carefully so as not to fall down the cliff (if you do, no biggie, there’s a path that will let you climb back up easily). From the top you should be able to see the next objective, a Mound of Dirt, so jump over that way and turn in the quest, picking up “Wet job.”

Time to continent-hop again. You’re going back to Eastern Kingdoms, this time to Loch Modan. For Alliance, this is a short-ish run, and not a dangerous one. You can either start in Ironforge and walk south through Dun Morogh into Loch Modan, or go from Stormwind via boat at Menethil Harbor to Wetlands, and then had southeast through the mountain tunnel into Loch Modan.

Horde, this is another rough one. You’ll need to start in Undercity and run through Tirisfall Glades, exiting to the southwest into Silverpine Forest. Follow the path further south into Hillsbrad Foothills, continuing east into Arathi Highlands, across the southern bridge into Wetlands, and then finally through the mountain tunnel into Loch Modan. You will absolutely run into Alliance guards along the way and have to deal with PvP, there’s no way around it. Just corpse-run when you can and do your best.

Either way, you’ll want to end up at the Stonewrought Dam, which is at the very north end of the eponymous Loch of Loch Modan. You’ve got to climb atop the dam itself and walk across until you see a campsite of sorts on a ledge overlooking Wetlands. Once you’re in the right spot, descend onto the ledge above the stone heads and interact with the Eagle Figurine to complete your quest and pick up the next one, “Eagle’s Fist.”

Just one more step to go, and fortunately, it’s not too far away. Horde and Alliance alike will want to head north, back through Wetlands and Arathi Highlands toward Hillsbrad Foothills. On the border between Arathi and Hillsbrad is the Thoradin Wall, and this is your destination. Follow the wall north until you see a broken cart. The cart is on the Hillsbrad side of the wall, but this is a little easier to do at lower levels if you walk up the Arathi side and then go through the gap in the wall near the cart to cross over, as there are no monsters on the Arathi side.

You can use that cart to climb up the wall. There’s a bit of a platforming puzzle here. First climb on the weird cylinder thing, jump to the board that’s jutting out on the side, then up the cart to the wall. Then just follow the path you can take up the crumbling wall stones (start your climb on the low far left stone) until you see the camp ahead of you. Interact with the hanging Messenger Bag to finish “Eagle’s Fist” and pick up “This Must Be the Place.” Then, click on the Hastily Rolled-up Satchel to finish the last quest and get your sleeping bag at last. Congrats!

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I spend a lot of time keeping up with the 2026 movie schedule and all the upcoming superhero movies, but Jennifer Garner left me thinking about a Batman production from a decade ago. The actress recently shared a fond memory involving Ben Affleck, Ina Garten and an unforgettable family trip to Paris. I love that the Caped Crusader barely scratches the surface of what made it so special.

During a conversation on Happy Hour with Ina Garten, the 13 Going on 30 actress recalled taking her children overseas while Affleck was filming in London. Apparently, the comic book movie production provided the perfect excuse to get out of town for a while. Garner explained:

When my kids were little, I went to Paris. Ben was shooting some Batman-ish movie in London, and we went for six weeks. I took them out of school. It was the last time I really took kids out of school, but it was wonderful. It was incredible. It was so fun.

I recently revisited Affleck and Garner's time making Daredevil together, so hearing her describe his later superhero blockbuster as some "Batman-ish movie" is especially funny. I imagine Affleck had a few more specific words for the project, but I appreciate Garner remembers the family adventure rather than whatever Bruce Wayne was getting up to at the time.

Her timing also helps identify the film. While Justice League arrived in theaters in 2017, Affleck and the production spent months filming in London the previous year. Reports from that April confirmed that Garner and their three children planned to stay in the U.K. during production. By May, the family had also been spotted vacationing in Paris. So, despite the wonderfully vague description, Justice League appears to be our Batman-ish culprit.

There's a bittersweet wrinkle to the timeline. Garner and Affleck announced their separation in 2015, before the trip, and officially filed for divorce in 2017. Their divorce was finalized the following year. That makes this a particularly sweet memory of their family life during a complicated period. The two have maintained a close co-parenting relationship since, with Garner recently praising Affleck for helping care for their children while she works.

Apparently, we have Ina Garten to thank for one of Garner's favorite memories from the trip. With her youngest son, Samuel, only 4 at the time, Garner shared photos of the kids with Garten, who suggested they take a boat ride along the Seine. Really, who am I to argue with the Barefoot Contessa about how to spend an afternoon in Paris?

Garner recalled cruising down the river as the city began lighting up around them, and the experience stuck with her. She's since made a point of doing it whenever she returns to Paris, and looking back at those original photos still reminds her of how happy the kids were. She told Garten that her suggestion made the whole thing "such an adventure." I love that something as simple as taking a boat ride became one of those family memories she keeps coming back to.

Garten's Paris recommendations didn't stop there. Years later, when Garner returned with her eldest daughter Violet, she texted her friend for another round of suggestions. This time Garten sent them to a handbag boutique, a cheese shop, a specialty food market and a restaurant specializing in soufflés. Violet apparently enjoyed the itinerary so much that she retraced their steps while studying abroad. Now I'm wondering how I get Ina Garten's number before my next vacation.

I like hearing Garner speak so fondly about those days, especially knowing what was happening in her personal life at the time. It also makes me wonder how many wonderful family memories get made while Hollywood's biggest productions happen in the background.

Affleck might have been busy bringing his take on The Dark Knight to life; his wife and kids were apparently having an adventure all their own. Something tells me those Paris photographs mean a whole lot more to her than another superhero movie ever could.

Death Stranding 2! Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii! Atomfall!

Sony's revealed the second wave of games coming to PlayStation Plus Premium and Extra this month, and there are some genuine big-name attractions, led by Hideo Kojima's futuristic delivery man showstopper Death Stranding 2: On the Beach.

Here's the new games coming PlayStation Plus Extra and Premium in November:

And here are a couple of games coming only to PlayStation Plus Premium in November:

There's a lot to recommend in that list. Death Stranding 2 was one of the standout games of 2025. "A busier, louder, and more emotionally resplendent take on this singular hiking sim," Lewis Gordon wrote in Eurogamer's Death Stranding 2 review.

Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii also shone brightly last year, as ridiculous as it was. "A raucous, absurd spin-off that manages to still feel like a first-rate Yakuza game despite the leftfield setting and delightfully unhinged plot," wrote Matt Elliott in Eurogamer's Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii review.

Meanwhile, Atomfall - Rebellion's quirky British take on a Fallout-like post-apocalyptic idea - was awarded three out of five stars. "If you can get over a difficult start and fancy a lean take on the survival genre, Atomfall delivers an intriguing tale worth discovering," Tom Orry wrote in Eurogamer's Atomfall review. It's presumably been significantly patched and smoothed since then.

The Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake also scored three out of five stars. "Some excellent enhancements make this the ultimate version of Dragon Quest 3, but it could still do more to make it wholly welcoming to newcomers," Daniella Lucas wrote in Eurogamer's Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D review.

We didn't review Hell Let Loose, but the popular World War 2 shooter would go on to amass a serious following and spawn a follow-up game in Hell Let Loose: Vietnam recently, which we did review. "The lavish jungles, rigid command structure, and emphasis on communication make Hell Let Loose: Vietnam a fascinating war simulator when it works. But its many variables can all too easily devolve into a miserable snipe-fest," Rick Lane wrote.

There's plenty to be getting on with, then.

Sony also announced in the PlayStation Blog post it's retiring the PS Plus app on PC from 10th December. Why? Because nobody really uses it.

"With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4 percent) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use," Sony wrote. "As a result, the PlayStation Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available."

#3671. It’s A Relief To Go Back To The Simple Joy Of Ocarina Of Time After A Decade Of Being Overwhelmed By Breath Of The Wild

The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the WildThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of TimeThe Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom

My friends, put the tomatoes down. I havenât even gotten to speak yet. I, like most people who own a Nintendo Switch 2 and are killing time until Grand Theft Auto 6 launches next week, am playing The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and Iâm having a pretty good time going back to a game that was once an elementary school obsession for me, especially because itâs been a long time since I really felt a constant sense of progression in a Zelda game after a decade of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom.

Yeah, the game is incredibly simple by modern standards, and Nintendo has done a lot to ensure that by making the game demonstrably easier in dozens of small ways that add up, but I think that relative simplicity is what draws me to it. Iâve been chipping away at the game in short sessions, usually finishing a temple or two before putting it down for the rest of the day, and the tangible feeling of momentum is what keeps me coming back to it just about every other evening at this point.

Over the years, especially with the rise of open-world games, I have identified that I am a goal-oriented person when it comes to how a video game can hold my attention. Thereâs just so much competition for whatever spare hours I have that if the bulk of my time playing a game is spent getting to the things I care about, I can lose interest fairly quickly. I want to see where the story goes, I want to reach the end of a quest line, and I loathe tedious open-world traversal more than most video game activities.Â

I canât entirely avoid open-world games in 2026, but if a game doesnât have a quick or engaging way to get around a giant map, it actively deters me from playing it. I often cite the Infamous series, with all its superpowered movement and interesting environmental interactions, as a great example of a game that makes its open-world map tolerable to me. A car or a horse is probably not going to cut it. There are exceptions from time to time, such as Cyberpunk 2077âs Night City entrancing me so much that Iâd gladly take in the view as I drove around on my motorcycle. But if I can help it, I want to spend my limited gaming time on things that arenât simply moving from one side of a giant space to another.

Breath of the Wild and its excellent sequel, Tears of the Kingdom do a lot to break up the tedium of simply moving through a space. The survival sim-esque friction and gizmo-building mechanics are brilliant evolutions of the original Zelda formula, and Nintendoâs ability to still draw water from the well of a decades-old franchise is commendable. I really enjoyed my time with both games, despite them grinding against a lot of my ingrained gaming sensibilities. The puzzles in the shrines, the constant feeling of discovery in its giant open world, and the colorful casts of weirdos and heroes you meet throughout the games maintain all that same Zelda spirit, but with a meaningful expansion of what a Zelda game looks like.Â

But man, is it a relief to go back to Ocarina of Time. I want puzzle-solving and discovery that I can get to quickly, that doesnât need me to meaningfully prep a survival bag so I can trek to the other side of the map while hoping my melee weapons can last me the whole trip, and what Ocarina is delivering feels downright breezy. Iâm sorry, Iâm sorry. I know itâs regressive of me to say Iâd like for the series to strip away all the cool things itâs done in the past nine years, but I havenât had a Zelda experience that feels like this in so long. The top-down 2D games are similar (at least those that came after the pretty open-ended and opaque original game), but they donât have the targeting and swordplay of the postâOcarina of Time era that rounds out the vision I have of what makes a 3D Zelda game.

I donât really hold any illusions that Zelda is going to go back to the structure of Ocarina of Time, but it is refreshing to be handed the tools I need to accomplish things without worrying that my weapon is going to break from battle damage or that Iâll run out of some vital consumable before I reach my goal. The Legend of Zelda is gonna be fine no matter where it goes moving forward, but for as dated and small in scope as Ocarina of Time might feel compared to Tears of the Kingdom, it sure does remind me that there was once a time when I didnât feel like I was fighting against the elements just to get to where I wanted to go.

Capcom still hasn't announced a release date for Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance, the Sunbreak-scale DLC that was revealed in February, but it seems like we might be getting a chance to sample the expansion before too long. A recent Steam listing update has provided a strong reason to suspect that there'll be a public beta for Ascendance available ahead of its launch in 2027.

As SteamDB changelogs show, the Steam app entry for Monster Hunter Wilds' 2024 public beta was quietly updated early this morning to change the app's name from "Monster Hunter Wilds Beta test" to "Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance Beta test." Similarly, the listing's visual assets were updated to feature key art of a hunter facing an Arateka, one of the new monsters being introduced in the expansion.

And sure enough, while the Wilds beta was removed from player libraries after it ended, it's possible for users who'd previously played it to confirm its listing changes within the Steam app by viewing their own played games from their Steam profile. I just looked. It says Ascendance right there.

As the previous Wilds beta consisted of a repackaged demo build, it's likely that an Ascendance beta would follow suit: I'd expect a similar set of hunts to what in-person attendees were able to get hands-on time with at Tokyo Game Show in September, offering a chance to try out the new Boost Bracer weapon mechanics in Master Rank combat.

If a beta does materialize, it'll hopefully be a smoother experience than what beta hunters got in 2024. The early Wilds playtest was the first time PC players encountered the dreaded origami monsters, a symptom of the severe optimization issues that tanked Wilds' reputation for over a year after launch.

As for when that beta might be available, we can only speculate—but given that Monster Hunter has made prior appearances at Geoff Keighley productions, a public playtest that accompanies a hypothetical Game Awards trailer makes intuitive sense. But I'm just reading the tea leaves here—Capcom hasn't said a word about when it'll offer its next DLC teaser.

Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance is set to launch some time in 2027.

#3669. PlayStation Cancels Fairgames After Years Of Silence

Another one of PlayStation’s live-service games has crashed and burned, asÂ Fairgames, the company’s online shooter that was being developed by first-party PlayStation developer Haven Studios, has been canceled.

As reported by Bloomberg, Haven Studios isn’t undergoing any layoffs as a result of the cancelation, as “the studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities,” according to a statement provided to the publication by PlayStation. The decision comes after Fairgames‘ recent playtest didn’t live up to Sony’s internal expectations.

âWhile the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,â PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email to employees and verified by Bloomberg. âCombined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.â

FairgamesÂ was initially announced back in 2023, and was originally being led by Jade Raymond, known as a producer of the earlyÂ Assassin’s Creed games. Raymond left Haven Studios in 2025, though the project quietly continued development. We really haven’t heard much about the game since it was initially unveiled.

Haven Studios was initially founded in 2021, and Sony acquired the company in 2022 before it had even put out a game. Now, it sounds like those who had been working onÂ FairgamesÂ will support the development of other games by PlayStation studios.

Fairgames is the latest in a long line of live-service disasters for Sony as the company continues to greenlight and then cancel its various attempts at forever games. Perhaps most famously, the company removed multiplayer shooter Concord from storefronts and then subsequently shut down its developer, Firewalk Studios.

Despite all this, Sony is still adamant that live-service games are an important part of PlayStation’s future.

#3667. Mortal Kombat 2 Is Winning The Race To Become Mortal Kombat 2

What's in a name? That's the question that Mortal Kombat studio CCO Ed Boon is asking, as he recently set up a few polls asking for opinions on what the next Mortal Kombat game should be called. According to Boon, three possible names were on the table: Mortal Kombat 12, Mortal Kombat 13, or Mortal Kombat 2.

"Footnote: Some people are assuming the title with the most votes will determine where we take the story," Boon wrote online. "That’s not the case. We’ve just had difficulty kounting lately."

The current naming convention for Mortal Kombat doesn't make much sense if you've taken a break from the franchise. The series made a successful comeback in 2011 with Mortal Kombat, the ninth installment in the franchise. This was followed by Mortal Kombat X in 2015 and Mortal Kombat 11 in 2019, which brought the original storyline that began in 1992's Mortal Kombat to a close. This was followed by a soft reboot in 2023 with Mortal Kombat 1, which remixed established story beats and put familiar characters in new roles.

To make things even more confusing, Mortal Kombat 1 heavily references multiple timelines toward the end of its campaign, drawing in characters from across a Mortal Kombat multiverse for a final showdown against Shang Tsung from the previous timeline. The Khaos Reigns expansion would also touch on these ideas, as the Titan version of Havik sought to merge all timelines into one.

Currently, "Mortal Kombat 2" is leading the votes with 45.2% of people polled by Boon favoring that title, at the time of writing. If this becomes the title of the next Mortal Kombat game, it will be the second Mortal Kombat 2, which will probably confuse anyone who hasn't been following along. While it hasn't been officially revealed yet, Boon did confirm that Mortal Kombat developer NetherRealm Studios is "pursuing another Mortal Kombat game," and he added that "other forms of media and whatnot" for the Mortal Kombat franchise are in development.

That was back in May, and since then, Mortal Kombat's parent company, Warner Bros. Interactive, has seen some big changes. Paramount’s $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery eventually went through, leading to the merger between Warner Bros. Interactive and Paramount Games Studio. That new entity puts Mortal Kombat, Game of Thrones, Batman, and a treasure trove of IP under the same roof as Avatar: The Last Airbender, South Park, and Star Trek. Tony Driscoll, president of games and experiences at Skydance, will oversee the new division.

#3666. You Can Play GTA 6 On A 13-Year-Old Xbox And It’ll Run At The Same Framerate As PS5 Pro

GTA 6PS5 ProXbox Cloud GamingXbox Series X/S

Grand Theft Auto 6 is only coming to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S at launch, but that doesn’t mean those consoles will be the only places to play it. Technically, fans who are still on Xbox One, which came out back in 2013, will also have a shot at exploring Rockstar Games’ latest version of Vice City thanks to Xbox Cloud Gaming.

Microsoft revealed the surprise last-gen perk in an update to its cloud gaming program this week. “Grand Theft Auto VI will be playable on day one through Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S, starting at 1am ET,” the company announced. “That means more players can experience one of the most anticipated games of the year on the consoles they already own. The game uses Xbox Series S graphics settings when cloud-streamed with Xbox Cloud Gaming.”

Series S graphics settings include the game running at a targeted 30fps framerate, the same as what will be available to players on Xbox Series X and PS5, as well as PS5 Pro. Sony’s more powerful hardware will still give players access to improved image quality with PSSR, but the game won’t run at 60fps anywhere, at least not at launch.

So what do you need in order to play GTA 6 on an Xbox One? Well, you’ll still need to own a digital copy of the game, which costs $80 and began pre-loading this week. You’ll also need access to Xbox Cloud Gaming, either via a Game Pass subscription or via Ã  la carte pricing. Ten hours of cloud gaming time in Vice City will cost Xbox owners $4.

What you won’t be able to do is stream GTA 6 to a mobile device or PC. Those options, which are a standard part of the rest of Xbox Cloud Gaming’s offerings, are excluded from the streaming agreement with Rockstar. It’s unclear if that’s a functionality that may be added sometime down the road after the game has been out for a while. GTA 6 will also support remote play on both Xbox and PS5, meaning you can stream it to other screens locally, including the PS Portal.

“Weâre excited to bring Grand Theft Auto 6 to more Xbox players at launch, and we will also be adding more titles from Rockstar Games to Xbox Cloud Gaming including Grand Theft Auto 5, Red Dead Redemption 2, and more in the coming months,” Microsoft added in today’s announcement.

I have no idea how many Xbox Ones are still out in the wild, or how many people may be tempted to blow the dust off of them instead of upgrading to a current-gen console. But given the ongoing price hikes for both the PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, it’s a really nice option for those who can’t otherwise afford to buy new hardware this fall for GTA 6.

#3665. GTA 6 Preloading Is Officially Live, Files Mention Multiplayer And PS5 Pro Features

At long last, you can now install Grand Theft Auto 6 on your console via preloading, or at least you can if you live in Australia or New Zealand. Preloading begins in all regions at midnight local time, so people in the US are almost there.

With preloading now live, people have dug through the files and found things they weren't intended to see. That includes references to things like "join Session," "launch Activity," and "launch Multiplayer Activity." People are taking these to be references to a new form of GTA Online.

Rockstar has said GTA 6 is a single-player game, but it’s expected to add some form of online multiplayer at some point. Just because "Multiplayer" was found in the game's files, that doesn't necessarily mean online functionality will be available at launch--it's likely coming sometime later.

People have theorized that GTA 6's story and Online could be separate games. That remains to be seen, but those who have the game preloaded have discovered that GTA 6's "Story" is an individual download within the game's files. Whatever the case, experts and insiders believe GTA 6's new online experience will launch at some point in 2027.

Additionally, the datamining effort led to some discoveries about what Rockstar might be cooking up in terms of PS5 Pro support. People believe they found references to 120Hz support on PS5 Pro, along with multi-frame super resolution, which is known as PSSR on PS5 Pro.

Rockstar has yet to announce any specifics about GTA 6 for PS5 Pro, and the game's trailers so far have been captured on a standard PS5.

While we’ve been patiently awaiting news on Shang-Chi 2, Marvel is bringing back Simu Liu for the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday. So, like many other MCU stars awaiting Secret Wars filming, the man has been trying to stay fit. He recently took a note from Inde Navarette when it comes to Marvel workouts, and trolled Saturday Night Live’s recent Shane Gillis gaffe in the same video.

I’m sure Marvel was super happy about getting roped in to the Shane Gillis monologue controversy, which involved the Tires star joking about women wearing little clothing at the gym these days. (He also capped these comments by calling them “whores,” which is probably what made the story go as viral as it did.) Anyway, Shane Gillis made the joke at Studio 8H, and then a week later Inde Navarette referenced it while talking about working out to play one of the X-Men in her own SNL monologue.

This is where Simu Liu comes in. The man came out of the wood work this week to cheekily show off a gym workout. He superimposed the video with Inde Navarette’s SNL monologue comments, and captioned the video, “time to put on my little outfit…”

Listen, this isn’t the first time Simu Liu has had a little fun trolling on the Internet, and I feel confident in guessing it won’t be the last. Just a couple of months ago he had a little fun with the MCU movies in order, and asked fans to “please help [him] support this little indie feature,” above a poster for Avengers: Doomsday, which will likely make over a billion dollars. Then, there was that time he joked about the Spider-Man leaks when Andrew Garfield and Tobey Maguire were involved in one of Tom Holland's popular films.

He can take it as well as dish it out, though. Early in his career, he modeled for some stock photos, and the Internet LOVES to bring it up. But he's taken the comments on the chin.

Right now, Marvel is in between films, so if you’re going to troll about the MCU, now’s a good time for a star to get a little attention for it. While schlepping relatively low weights is not as impressive as, say, one-armed pull-ups, it’s a good way to keep the fanbase engaged as Doomsday gets closer.

Avengers: Doomsday hits the 2026 release schedule around the holidays, and is in theaters opposite Dune 3, which has earned it the moniker Dunesday. Meanwhile, Chris Hemsworth has remained swole, and it has people wondering if he’s getting ready for Secret Wars. On the other hand, Simu Liu has already confirmed he's in both.
